Definition: Affordability of mobile broadband data, measured as the cost of a basic mobile data plan (1-2GB) as a percentage of GNI per capita. The UN Broadband Commission target is below 2% of monthly GNI per capita. Affordability is the single largest barrier to internet adoption in Africa.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: World Bank Gambia Digital Economy Diagnostic (2021, using pre-2021 ITU/PURA pricing) records 1GB mobile data at USD1.80/month, equal to 1.5% of monthly GNI per capita, which falls in the 'Affordable (1-2%)' band rather than 'Moderate (2-5%)'. No fresher ITU ICT Price Basket figure for Gambia could be located, so this remains dated evidence — recommend human review to confirm against 2024/2025 data.

Definition: The country's total international internet bandwidth capacity per internet user, indicating the quality and capacity of the country's connection to the global internet. Determined by submarine cable landings (for coastal states), cross-border terrestrial fibre (for landlocked states), and satellite links.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Only historical ITU-sourced data could be found (2012-2016, averaging 4.58 kbit/s per user, peaking at 10.93 kbit/s in 2016); no current per-user bandwidth figure was located via ITU DataHub or TeleGeography despite searching. Given the data is roughly a decade stale and infrastructure has since expanded (new fibre/data centre investment), the original 'Low (5-19 kbit/s)' score cannot be confirmed — recalculated as Unknown/n.a.; flagged for human review to obtain a current ITU figure.

Definition: Percentage of mobile connections using smartphones (as opposed to feature phones or basic phones). Smartphones are the minimum device requirement for accessing most digital public infrastructure services, apps, and mobile internet.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: No Gambia-specific smartphone adoption percentage could be verified. GSMA's Sub-Saharan Africa regional average smartphone adoption was only 42% in 2023 (forecast 69% by 2030; Africa-wide circa 63% in 2025); DataReportal only reports the share of 'broadband-capable' (3G/4G/5G) mobile connections (88.7-92.3%), which is not the same metric as smartphone share. The original '80%+' claim has no supporting country-level source and is inconsistent with regional benchmarks; recalculated as Unknown, flagged for human review.

Definition: The availability and presence of major cloud service providers (hyperscale and regional) operating in or serving the country with local or near-local infrastructure. Cloud availability determines access to scalable computing resources for government, business, and startups.
Value Name: Served remotely from distant regions only (>100ms latency)
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Confirmed that no hyperscale provider is local to Gambia — the nearest AWS (af-south-1, Cape Town) and Azure (South Africa North/West) regions are thousands of kilometres away in a different sub-region, supporting the original score of 2 despite it originally being unsourced. Note the April 2026 QGroup/Huawei data-centre launch is reported to include new local 'cloud computing services', but details are too sparse to justify an upgrade on this source alone; flagged for human review as the position may soon change.

redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.

Definition: The country's performance on the WIPO Global Innovation Index (GII), which measures innovation capabilities across institutions, human capital, infrastructure, market sophistication, business sophistication, knowledge outputs, and creative outputs. Provides a composite view of the national innovation ecosystem.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Gambia does not appear in the GII 2024 economy profiles/rankings (133 economies), nor is it named among the Sub-Saharan African countries WIPO highlights in its own results summary (Mauritius, South Africa, Botswana, Cabo Verde, Senegal, Kenya, Zambia, Benin, Mauritania, Burundi, Rwanda, Madagascar, Togo, Uganda); the same absence holds across the 2019-2023 editions reviewed. The original 'rank 121+' claim is unsupported — recalculated as 'Unknown/n.a. (not included in GII)' per the metadata scale.

Definition: The maturity of the country's technology startup ecosystem, based on the number of tech startups, venture capital activity, accelerators/incubators, and the presence of a supportive ecosystem. Africa's startup scene is well-documented by trackers like Partech, Disrupt Africa, and Briter Bridges.
Value Name: Nascent (very few tech startups, no visible VC activity)
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Tracxn identifies 185 Gambian startups (17 funded, concentrated in banking/fintech) and two active incubators (The Hub Ltd, est. 2019; Startup Incubator Gambia, est. 2015, reporting over 50 startups supported), but no material venture funding rounds for Gambia are tracked by Disrupt Africa, Partech Africa or Africa: The Big Deal. This is more consistent with 'Emerging (some startups, limited funding, 1-2 hubs)' (code 2) than 'Nascent'; recalculated accordingly, though funding totals are not independently confirmed — recommend human review.

revision_notes: No clean ITU household-survey percentage for Gambia's basic digital literacy was located; the World Bank diagnostic notes only 15% of in-school adolescent boys (2% out-of-school) report ICT skills, and the 2018 MICS shows 19% household computer ownership — both broadly consistent with a low (10-24%) population-wide estimate but not a direct confirmation. Original code left unchanged pending a precise, dated ITU/DEN figure; recommend human review.

redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: GSMA's Mobile Gender Gap Reports (2024/2025) survey a fixed set of roughly 12-14 low- and middle-income countries and Gambia does not appear to be one of them; no Gambia-specific ITU gender-disaggregated internet-use figure was found either. The original 'moderate gap (20-29%)' claim has no identifiable source; recalculated as Unknown/n.a., flagged for human review to source Gambia-specific data (e.g. GBoS or Afrobarometer).
